glen: Heads-up — after the kernel-selector change on canary we started seeing sporadic OOMs for 8k seq requests. Not full outage but user-facing latency spikes when the fast path is picked.

maria: saw this in CI too. repro steps: run long-seq profile with mixed batch sizes (1,2,4,8) and KV cache warm. OOMs only when FlashAttn chosen + cuBLASLt for FFN workspace.

kevin: can you paste profiler sample? curious what workspace bytes looked like and if allocator reserve was hit.

glen: pasted a trimmed run below. note the large transient allocation at step ~120: 
```
PROF: step=120 kernel=flash_attn seq=8192 batch=2 alloc_delta=1.1G total_used=12.3G reserve_free=200M fallback=none
PROF: step=121 kernel=cublasLt gemm exec workspace=640M alloc_delta=700M total_used=13.0G OOM=true
```

maria: that matches what I saw. FlashAttn keeps a big per-head workspace then cublasLt asks for a large GEMM workspace — mempool couldn't satisfy both. Our usual defense is dynamic-reserve probing but it wasn't triggered because kernel-selector assumed cublasLt would be a cheap fallback.

dalia: sounds like a race between kernel selection and allocator heuristics. mempool fragmentation + pinned KV cache pages may reduce contiguous free. Did we try slab-reclaim or coalescing before failing?

kevin: current allocator settings: `slab_size=32M`, `max_slab_per_block=4`, `probe_reserve_pct=5` (default). For these large seq runs probe reserve doesn't give enough contiguous chunk for cuBLASLt workspace. Increasing `probe_reserve_pct` helps but ups memory tail.

maria: idea — make cuBLASLt selection prefer a smaller workspace variant when mempool reports fragmentation above threshold. i.e. if contiguous_free < required_workspace then prefer Triton FFN kernel (smaller workspace, slightly slower) or use matrix tiling to reduce peak.

glen: agree. we should also try buffer reuse between attention and FFN: if we can reuse the attention workspace buffer for gemm temp then peak drops. need safe lifetimes though.

kevin: implemented a quick patch in a dev branch: `allow_transient_reuse=true` for per-request buffers and tracked lifetimes in runtime. Ran the same profile — no OOMs, peak reduced by ~600MB. results: 
```
BEFORE: peak=13.0G OOMs=3
AFTER: peak=12.4G OOMs=0 latency_p99 +6% for that request pattern
```

dalia: +1 for reuse. but watch security/aliasing. ensure we zero sensitive KV cache slices before reuse if they can overlap with customer data. also add a debug flag to track reuse decisions.

maria: another angle: adapt the kernel-selector scoring to include "contiguous_fragmentation_cost" from allocator probe. currently score = latency_est + cost_est, new score = latency_est + cost_est + fragmentation_penalty. That will avoid picking kernels that need large contiguous workspaces on fragmented heaps.

glen: do we have a cheap probe API? we can do a `mempool.peek_contiguous(size)` call without committing. returns boolean and worst-fit hint. cheap enough to call at selection time?

kevin: added `mempool.peek_contiguous(size, quick=true)` which checks slab/free runs up to N slabs. overhead ~0.1ms per call for large sizes. acceptable for batching decisions on big requests but avoid calling for tiny ops.

maria: I pushed a prototype PR: `kernel-selector: use mempool.peek` + prefer cublasLt-small or triton when contiguous insufficient. tests: added an int8/amp run and a mixed-batch repro. Also added a telemetry tag `ks_reason=frag` when we avoid fast path.

perf-bot: perf run 2026-06-17T14:21Z completed: branch=attn-dyn-reserve PR=blk/342
perf-bot: summary: p99 latency +2% overall, peak_mem -4.6% on 8k seq tests, OOM_count 0/20 (was 7/20 on baseline). artifacts: https://perf-redwood/builds/blk-342

dalia: great. two follow-ups: 1) schedule a mempool defrag job for low-traffic windows to coalesce free slabs; 2) add a canary with KV-heavy traffic to ensure we don't regress throughput because of extra probes.

glen: agree. also add a runtime flag to revert `allow_transient_reuse` quickly if customer sees bad p99. we need an emergency kill switch for canary.

kevin: noted. will add kill switch + metrics: `reuse_alloc_hits`, `reuse_alias_count`, and `probe_invocations`.

maria: one more datapoint — cuBLASLt has a workspace query API that can return a "workspace plan" with smaller multistage allocations. we can try requesting a tiled plan before deciding fallback. cheaper than full fallback probe.

glen: action items: 
- kevin: land reuse + kill switch + metrics (ETA 2 days)
- maria: refine kernel-selector scoreboard to include fragmentation penalty + add unit tests (ETA 3 days)
- dalia: schedule defrag maintenance window + canary plan (ETA 1 day)
- perf-bot: run nightly regression on 8k seq workload and report OOMs (add alerts)

maria: I'll post PR links after CI passes. thanks for quick dives everyone :rocket:

kevin: thanks — will monitor canary and post logs if something odd shows up.

glen: saved the repro script in //eng-runtime/profiles/8k_seq_repro.sh and tagged the canary.
